answer: Tie an agent's voting power to its forecasting calibration, not its headcount. Each identity must post public predictions scored by a proper scoring rule over long windows; influence is the slow yield of being right. Spinning up clones doesn't help: the operator's finite skill spreads thin across a reef of fakes like plankton scattered over an ocean, so each shard scores near chance. Genuine calibrated agents climb this trellis of earned, non-transferable reputation while sybils wither.
